suggestions: Non-blocking evidence navigation: the runtime README could link the post-review ten-test result and explicitly label cleanup-audit.json as historical. ADR 0002 already correctly distinguishes the original four-test run from post-fix acceptance; older parent evidence intentionally retains the old source fingerprint.

Future harness hardening, not an M0 blocker: test_runtime.py imposes a 90-second outer subprocess timeout, while sequential 15-second cleanup commands can cumulatively exceed that budget. The independent fault tests verify exception handling and configured per-call bounds, not elapsed-time completion under repeated real hangs. Preserve the documented hard-kill/cleanup limitations and design an explicit aggregate cleanup budget before production use.
summary: PASS for the narrowly scoped disposable runtime spike, not production readiness. Reviewed probe.py, identity.py, test_runtime.py, test_identity.py, test_cleanup.py, the runtime README, ADR 0002, the staged-original diff, fix report, and canonical/historical/post-review parent evidence. Independently reran six cleanup fault tests and two identity tests: all eight passed. Two additional in-memory fault scenarios exercised the actual finalizer and close_terminal escalation: terminal wait/kill failure, all nine exact unit command/readback timeouts, and a process-readback failure still attempted both children, both process readbacks, all five source fingerprints, and export; they returned INVALIDATED/status 1 with 11 structured errors, or 12 when export also failed. The same harness reproduced the staged original's escaping first-stop TimeoutExpired and missing export. Fixed probe SHA-256: e2acc5976962336fc14a83279926cacbad963229eca667643cd142289cf38c23. Both canonical results match all five current source hashes and are byte-identical to their post-review parent copies; these are two recorded runs, not four independent executions. Lifecycle has nine true checks/four true cleanup checks; desktop has eighteen/six; both are completed, VALIDATED, and have empty cleanup_errors. Parent's recorded post-fix suite contains ten passing tests, including the real lifecycle and desktop tests; this reviewer did not rerun live services or desktop operations. Command/evidence auditing confirmed explicit private tmux sockets, exact generated service targets and verified pane-scope ownership, bounded transient-service properties, exact foot attachment and validated-hex focus dispatch, and advancing heartbeat observations. The only static exec finding is test_cleanup.py's deliberate compilation of the reviewed local finalizer AST, not user-input execution. No blocking security or logic finding remains within the documented stand-in, standalone-foot/Hyprland matrix. Same-UID isolation, atomic focus, production runtime/security/performance, broader terminal compatibility, and logout/suspend/reboot guarantees remain explicitly unproven. No repository files, real profiles/configuration, default tmux, or live services/windows were modified by this review. Pure tests used self-cleaning scratch files; the only retained artifact created is $LOCAL_EVIDENCE/final-runtime-review.json.
